bull.b: Strong revenue growth combined with very high gross margins indicates attractive product economics and expanding commercial traction. If Harrow sustains demand across its ophthalmic portfolio, the business can generate increasing gross profit to support sales investment, development programs, and eventual operating leverage.

Growth across several products reduces reliance on a single commercial driver and demonstrates broadening adoption in dry eye, surgical, and ophthalmic care markets. Rising prescriptions, ordering accounts, and surgical demand provide a durable base for continued portfolio expansion over the next several quarters.

The TYRVAYA acquisition expands Harrow’s dry-eye franchise with an already approved therapy, additional commercial talent, and established distribution access. Integrating the product into Harrow’s existing infrastructure could broaden customer reach and create meaningful recurring revenue alongside VEVYE.

bear.b: A more debt-funded balance sheet reduces financial flexibility if operating performance weakens and increases the importance of sustained cash generation. Higher leverage can also constrain investment choices, raise refinancing exposure, and make future funding more difficult or potentially dilutive.

Harrow’s strong gross margin has not yet translated into consistent profitability because operating costs and other headwinds remain substantial. Negative quarterly EBITDA and rising commercial spending increase execution pressure, particularly as the company adds integration costs and must convert demand into earnings.

Meeting annual guidance requires a sizable second-half acceleration across product growth, channel normalization, salesforce productivity, and integration. Reimbursement loss in ASC settings adds a structural commercial obstacle, making the forecast dependent on successful in-office-market expansion and disciplined execution.
